risk.line: Held at HIGH, but the character of the risk changed overnight. Yesterday the board was an argument about whether an unverified Iranian claim was true; tonight it is a live exchange with an unpaid debt on it. The US struck IRGC rocket launchers on Larak, Iran answered with ballistic missiles at two US air bases in Jordan and a drone into Emirati waters, both largely intercepted, and Trump has publicly promised to "hit them very hard" without naming a size. That promise is the escalation risk, not the volley - an unsized vow is either a campaign or a climbdown once it is cashed, and the equilibrium that has held all year depends on nobody being killed. We are not at CRIT because the falsifier has not fired: no confirmed American deaths, no struck US hull, no closure of the lane. Two structural moves sit underneath. CENTCOM's 28 August clearance announcement transferred ownership of the waterway's safety to Washington, so every future incident is now a US credibility problem. And at Asheville the United States restored Russia's seat at the G20 finance table on the same day it asked Europe to tighten the Iran siege - the concession and the ask are in the same room, which makes the ask more expensive. Off the main board, India has rejected a Hague ruling ordering it back into the Indus Waters Treaty, and China has warned Palau of "consequences" for hosting Taiwan's foreign minister.

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: RAISED +4, the day's biggest move. The month-long lull broke: the first publicly acknowledged US strike on Iranian territory since late July, Iranian retaliation against TWO third countries (missiles at US bases in Jordan, a drone at the UAE), and a president publicly posting AI video of Kharg - the terminal that ships about 90% of Iranian crude - being destroyed. The reference class here is RECURRENCE, not war initiation, and in that literature the hazard of renewed major fighting is highest immediately after a lull breaks rather than spread evenly across the horizon. Capped at +4 because CENTCOM called it limited and precise, Iran's reply was target-matched and intercepted, and the named November trigger still sits later in the window

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover past 50% of pre-war volume
forecasts.note: CUT 3. The party negotiating mine CLEARANCE at Muscat was caught preparing to lay more: CENTCOM says it hit the Larak launchers because Guards were readying rockets carrying sea mines for the international lanes, and the IRGC confirmed the strike and its casualties. That is a physical act inside the technical window, not a statement - the seventh near-breakthrough-then-condition cycle. Fortna's finding anchors it: corridors and ceasefires with no agreed third-party verifier hold materially worse, and there is still no published minesweeping calendar and no corridor coordinates. Held to 3 because the strike was deliberately small and because Gargash publicly called for shipping to be restored - a Gulf principal pushing the other way

forecasts.q: Brent stays inside the $80-100 band
forecasts.note: CUT 3, and deliberately NOT part of today's escalation cluster. Brent at 90.69, up 2.93%, is near-neutral for a double-barrier question - it sits about as far from the geometric mean of the 80 and 100 barriers as the 88.29 audit anchor did. This is purely a volatility re-rate: a broken lull plus a head of state publicly threatening the terminal that ships 90% of Iranian crude widens the distribution on both sides, and higher volatility lowers survival inside a fixed band regardless of direction

forecasts.q: US Hormuz concession within 30 days after the Xi summit
forecasts.note: CUT 2. Treasury moved the other way: Bessent told the AP he expects NEW secondary sanctions weekly, focused on banks, said this is going to be financial violence if we have to, and takes that to G20 finance ministers at Asheville on Monday - a publicly pre-committed escalating cadence running straight through the summit window. Escalation and concession are substitutes on one file, and Schelling's rule is that compellence needs a face-saving ladder; Washington just removed rungs from its own. Held to 2 because the concession this scores is post-summit by construction

forecasts.q: Saudi Arabia publicly moves toward enrichment or the bomb
forecasts.note: RAISED 1 - the named pathway acquired machinery. Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan held the first working meeting of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed on 7 August, with Ankara's foreign minister publicly canvassing expansion. Overt proliferation announcements are rare, which is why this number is low and structurally undercounts covert hedging - but institutional machinery reliably precedes announcement, and a standing trilateral committee including the Muslim world's only nuclear-armed state is the vehicle a sharing arrangement would surface through. Only 1 point: a first meeting is a calendar item, not a capability

forecasts.q: Hormuz at full pre-war normal
forecasts.note: HELD deliberately, and the non-move is the discipline. This runs off the same framework as today's GEO-001 cut at a harder bar, and moving both would spend one fact twice - the exact error the Aug 30 audit named. The falsifier stands: transits above 40 a day for two straight weeks before Oct 15 breaks the argument and sends both numbers back up

forecasts.q: Economic D-Day works: China cuts Iranian oil >50%, sustained
forecasts.note: Held despite a loud day. Bessent escalated INTENSITY - weekly designations, a G20 demand, financial violence - but Bloomberg reports the world mostly shrugged off the D-Day threat, and Drezner's point is precisely that intensity is not compliance: sanctions change behaviour about a third of the time at best and near zero against a great power on a core interest. The question asks about Beijing, and Beijing was not designated

forecasts.q: US sanctions a top-10 Chinese bank before the Xi summit
forecasts.note: Held at 7, with the two effects named. A weekly cadence adds draws, which pushes up; Bessent again said the next target is another bank and again did not say a Chinese one, which pushes down. Farrell and Newman's rule decides the tie: the hammer that hangs is worth more than the hammer that falls, and an enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive

forecasts.q: US commits to fixed Venezuelan heavy-crude export infrastructure
forecasts.note: Held under the stricter Aug 30 wording. Chevron expanding Petropiar into the Ayacucho 8 block and a 300,000 b/d export target by March are field-access and offtake items; this question needs an awarded dredging or terminal contract. Motive is untouched - premeditation is what this scores, and concrete is what would show it

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to US happens in September
forecasts.note: Held. Xi is in Bishkek for the SCO summit exactly as the calendar said he would be, which is a small confirmation of the staff-preparation signal rather than new information. Announced head-of-state visits with active sherpa work are consummated about 90% of the time

forecasts.q: IF a Hormuz deal happens, it preserves Iranian transit administration
forecasts.note: Held, and today strengthened the mechanism without moving the number. Ostovar's thesis is that the IRGC converts crisis into permanent institution; an organisation that answers a strike on its minelayers within hours is demonstrating that transit control is its institutional property, not a bargaining chip the foreign ministry can trade

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: Held. Bishkek changes nothing here: about 79% of interstate wars end within two years and Ukraine at 4.5 years is deep in the tail where the odds of stopping get lower, not higher. Summits between belligerents' patrons are not negotiations between belligerents

forecasts.q: Russian Q4 territorial gains fall below the Q2-Q3 average
forecasts.note: Held. Autumn mud then winter have historically depressed mechanized tempo against summer, before Kofman's manpower-crossover argument adds anything. ISW logged no Russian advances in the Novopavlivka and Oleksandrivka directions on Aug 28-29 and no ground activity reported at Pokrovsk on Aug 29 - consistent, not yet evidence

forecasts.q: Mojtaba makes a verified live public appearance
forecasts.note: Held. A day in which Iran's answer to a US strike was announced by the IRGC and its foreign ministry, with no word from the Leader on the most salient security event in a month, is consistent with the invisible-Leader model - but consistency is not new evidence and we do not re-count the same fact

forecasts.q: Fed's standing T-bill purchase program still running at end-2026
forecasts.note: Held. The exit got harder, not nearer: ON RRP at $0.17bn against a balance sheet at $6.73tn means there is no buffer to absorb a drain of short-end support. Facilities persist when the conditions that would justify ending them deteriorate

forecasts.q: Israel-Hezbollah escalates to multi-week campaign
forecasts.note: Held. Fortna is the anchor: ceasefires with an agreed third-party verifier hold materially better, and this framework still has none while the party being disarmed rejects the premise. The Oct 27 Israeli election is the constraint that prices it

forecasts.q: China quarantine or blockade of Taiwan
forecasts.note: Held. Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building, not the event. Allison is on record at under 1% for a blockade this year; Fravel and Mastro say the command purge pushed the kinetic timetable right

forecasts.q: US-China tariff truce collapses before Nov expiry
forecasts.note: Held. Negotiated truces rarely collapse before their own expiry while both parties are staging a summit inside the window, and the sanctions round that could have broken it named an Egyptian bank instead

forecasts.q: IF Ukraine fighting stops 30+ days pre-2028: armistice, no peace treaty
forecasts.note: Held. Stalemated interstate wars end in armistices far more often than in signed peace treaties - Korea 1953, Iran-Iraq 1988. If anything this is conservative

forecasts.q: Security-elite fracture in Iran (IRGC defection, coup, mass purge)
forecasts.note: Held. The decapitation-survival literature says security elites usually cohere, and a Corps that absorbs a strike and answers it within hours is cohering, not cracking. Takeyh's test needs a verified defection or purge

forecasts.q: China stands up a third physical-gold venue or a delivery-forcing mechanism
forecasts.note: Held. Gold volatility at 26.8, up 8.8% on the month, is stress in the paper market rather than venue construction - the distinction this question was cut for conflating last week. Reference class: two venues in twenty-four years

forecasts.q: Bitcoin's cycle top prints at or below ~$150k
forecasts.note: Held. The adoption-saturation model is untouched by this week's flow. Wide bars - Bitcoin has never traded through a real recession

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (NEW — the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Opens at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — 75% → 82%
hypotheses.d: Week's biggest mover, on three strands independent of the Israeli/exile channel. Pezeshkian said on Iranian state TV that communication with Khamenei is 'very difficult' — Tehran's own president, against his own interest. Washington routed its peace offer not to Araghchi but to Mohsen Rezaee, career IRGC commander-in-chief now running the security council. Cipher Brief: 'Tehran isn't saying who is actually in charge.' Capped at 82% because the state has promised footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders — that is the falsifier, and it is coming.

hypotheses.name: Nobody’s hurrying on Hormuz — HELD at 60%
hypotheses.d: The near-breakthrough-then-condition pattern fired a sixth time (Iran–Oman interim corridor and 30–60 days of technical talks, against Ghalibaf restating the full condition stack). Deliberately not moved: it is already priced, and a minesweeping calendar is what an honest process looks like too. The real test is live — the offer sits with the IRGC, so Tehran's answer is the experiment.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — 55% → 60%
hypotheses.d: The discriminating split signal arrived: PLA sorties kept declining while the coast guard escalated in kind — CCG 2307 pressing a Japanese coast guard ship in the strait Aug 6–10, which AEI reads as testing whether foreign vessels will obey PRC authority. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up is the ratchet signature. Capped at +5; the stated tell is what the coast guard does through the Sept 24 visit.

hypotheses.name: NEW · Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it opens at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts, and the reporting frames it in plain words as an alternative to Gulf oil routed through Hormuz. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Operation Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Mundane alternative, named and live: drugs, migration politics, regime-change, with the barrel a bonus. Falsifiers — cut hard if export volumes stay token (the $2-2.8bn tranches are a rounding error against control of 65bn bbl), if Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing does not actually swing off the Middle East, or if the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appears. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz, geography does not work that way — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Real Orinoco or Maracaibo channel-dredging and dedicated heavy-crude terminals WOULD be the premeditation tell. Unconfirmed today; it is the thing to watch.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — 45% → 52%
hypotheses.d: Economic Outcast hit ~60 teapots, tankers and traders and touched no Chinese state major and no bank — Treasury sent the majors a warning letter instead. Maximum pressure on Iran, calibrated to stop exactly short of anything that would detonate the Sept 24 summit. Held to +7 because the Munir offer is a real concession, and $4.10 gas before midterms is real evidence against premeditation.

hypotheses.name: NEW · A pre-announcement leak into oil futures
hypotheses.d: Four times in the war window, nine- and ten-figure short bets landed 15–20 minutes before an Iran announcement: ~$2.2bn across crude, gasoil and gasoline before Trump's Mar 23 pause post; ~$950m before the Apr 7 ceasefire; ~$760m before Iran said Hormuz would open. ~$7bn total; CFTC probing, four members of Congress demanding answers. Split: deliberate leak 45 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 25 / coincidence 10. This is the only entry in the book whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event rather than pattern-matched after — which is why it opens this high. Against it: no episode has surfaced around this week's diplomacy.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 30% → 25%
hypotheses.d: Cut again. The channels that actually moved this week were Oman, Pakistan and the new Mecca defence pact — Russia was absent from every one of them, and still has not offered the mediation this hypothesis expects. Motive 9/10, documentary evidence 0/10, pre-event evidence never. Cut to 15% if nothing surfaces by Sept 30.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Both its live predictions came in favourably this week and it gets credit for neither: the rival leverage hypothesis predicted the same things, and shared predictions are ambience. One more failed pre-summit call and it goes to the epitaph list.

brief.h: Trump says "we're going to hit them very hard" after Iranian missiles came at two US air bases in Jordan and a drone at the UAE - the month-long lull is over on both ledgers
brief.t: The sequence is confirmed and it runs in one direction. The US struck IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday, saying the Guards were readying rockets that deliver sea mines into the shipping lane. Iran answered overnight with ballistic missiles at two US air bases in Jordan and a drone into Emirati waters, both largely intercepted, and Trump told reporters "we're going to hit them very hard" and "there will be a response." One layer down is claim rather than fact: the IRGC says it brought down a US MQ-9 over the eastern strait, and no American confirmation exists. Oil rose on the exchange, which is the only part of this that has so far moved money.
brief.context: Name the mechanism: an announced clearance creates an obligation. On 28 August Admiral Brad Cooper said US forces had cleared the mines Iran laid in the internationally recognised lanes, citing nearly 1,500 commercial vessels escorted through carrying almost 750 million barrels. That statement was the moment of maximum credibility and also the moment Washington took ownership of the water - every incident from here is measured against a promise CENTCOM made. The deciding desk is not CENTCOM: it is the war-risk underwriter in London who reprices a hull on ambiguity alone, which is why Iran's cheapest remaining weapon is an unresolved claim rather than a hit. Base rate for this year: intercepted volleys with no confirmed deaths have twice produced a public vow, a limited answer, and then a lull of roughly a month. The equilibrium holds until somebody dies.

angles.effect: Buys a demonstration cheaply. Missiles fired at third countries and largely intercepted cost Iran little, killed no American, and still force Washington to answer - the point is the obligation to respond, not the damage.
Gains the licence it wanted and pays in commitment. "We're going to hit them very hard" is a promise with no stated size, and an unsized promise is either escalation or a climbdown once it is cashed.
Pay first and had no vote. Both absorbed fire aimed at American forces stationed on their soil in a quarrel neither is party to, and both now carry the domestic politics of hosting.
Carry the repricing. A resumed exchange days after a declared clearance is worth more to the war-risk premium than the clearance was ever worth in relief.

dec.kill: Confirmed American deaths, or a struck US-flagged hull, would break the intercepted-volley equilibrium and turn the vowed response into a campaign. An answer confined to more empty launchers on rocks, followed by another quiet month, confirms both sides are still buying the same demonstration.

brief.h: The White House finally names the counterparty: the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital takes a 35 percent stake in North American Blue Energy Partners, owned by Alejandro Betancourt
brief.t: This is the document our Venezuela card has been asking for, and it changes the story by supplying the one thing an announcement cannot fake - a name. NABEP receives 100-year rights over 17 fields holding about 65 billion proven barrels and has committed 100 billion dollars in new infrastructure; the State Department gets the right to buy 20 percent of output at cost; US citizens hold a majority of board seats and Washington keeps a veto over board members; Hegseth and Rubio signed. The White House says the arrangement is at "zero cost" to the United States. The load-bearing fact the slogan omits is who NABEP is: Betancourt chairs Derwick Associates, which won billions in emergency power contracts from 2009 and was scrutinised by investigators in Venezuela, the United States and Spain over suspected laundering of PDVSA funds - allegations he and the firm denied.
brief.context: Run the caveat protocol and the phrase that fails first is "zero cost." The Office of Strategic Capital exists to finance industries the Defence Department deems critical; it is a credit and equity desk, not a foreign-concession holder, and a 35 percent position plus a board veto is a sovereign commitment whether or not cash is appropriated this year. Time-to-delivery is the second constraint: 100 billion dollars of extra-heavy infrastructure in a country with a degraded grid is a three-to-seven year build, and Trump himself conceded it "could be a little bit" before pump prices move. The base rate on long concessions in Venezuela is the thing to hold onto - the state has nationalised foreign oil assets twice in living memory, so the exposure here is not the geology, it is the next government. The mechanism has a name: an equity stake is how a state converts a security guarantee into something that reads on the books as an asset.

angles.effect: Wins the largest concession in the hemisphere and, with it, legal rehabilitation. A businessman once inside a money-laundering investigation is now the Pentagon's joint-venture partner, which is a form of clearance no court granted.
Gains operating capital and an American principal with a financial interest in its survival - the exact thing sanctions were built to deny it - without ever publishing the headline 17-field pact.
Books a stake it may one day have to defend. Equity in fields inside a contested state is a commitment to their security, and that is the cost the zero-cost claim excludes.
Find themselves junior. The firms doing the contract-by-contract work now sit under a vehicle assembled in Washington rather than negotiated in the field.
Carries contingent sovereign, expropriation and security risk labelled as nothing. "No cost" is a statement about this year's appropriation, not about exposure.

dec.kill: Published joint-venture text naming the statutory authority under which OSC holds foreign equity, plus a first tranche of the 100 billion arriving from private capital with no federal guarantee, would let the zero-cost claim survive contact. A congressional request revealing a federal credit backstop, or the 100 billion never appearing on a signed financing document, confirms the cost was moved rather than removed.

brief.h: The United States, holding the G20 presidency, brought Anton Siluanov back to the finance table for the first time since 2022 - and European ministers refused to stand in the family photo
brief.t: Siluanov attended the Asheville meeting on Monday and held bilateral talks with Scott Bessent on Trump's Ukraine peace plan. Poland's Andrzej Domanski said "we do not trust Russia. They lie constantly, and you need to be really, really cautious." Germany's Lars Klingbeil called it a "signal I find troubling" and read it as "an attempt at normalisation." The White House's Kush Desai defended the meeting as working with Russia to "stop the endless bloodshed," and Bessent was reported making clear there would be no economic relief until the war ends. Separate the layers: the attendance is fact, the normalisation is inference, and no sanctions relief has been granted.
brief.context: The mechanism is chair discretion, and it is worth naming because most readers assume otherwise. Russia was never expelled from the G20 - the body has no expulsion procedure and no membership vote. What happened in 2022 was informal: Western ministers walked out, and the isolation was sustained by attendance rather than by rule. Anything sustained by attendance can be reversed by whoever writes the invitations, and this year that is the US Treasury. The sequencing is the real story: on the same day, at the same table, Bessent is asking these same ministers to sever their banks' remaining ties to Iran. Restoring a rail that costs you nothing and asking a favour in the same room is a recognisable negotiating structure - and Europe's price for the Iran ask just went up. Base rate: informal diplomatic exclusions reversed by a host tend to stay reversed, because the second restoration is never as costly as the first.

angles.effect: Recovers a seat for free. Four years of exclusion ended without a ceasefire, a withdrawal or a concession, and the precedent is now that the price of readmission is one friendly presidency.
Gains a venue for the Ukraine plan and pays in leverage on Iran. Every European minister asked to squeeze Tehran now has a fresh grievance to trade against that ask.
Pay in credibility they cannot recover. A refused photograph is the weakest instrument in diplomacy - it registers objection while conceding the room.
Carries the signalling cost. Normalisation of the finance channel is precisely the reassurance a state under negotiating pressure cannot afford its counterpart to receive early.
Genuinely gains on his own file, and this is the case where the cynical read and the constructive one point the same way: if a settlement needs a finance channel, one now exists.

dec.kill: Russia appearing in a joint communique, or a named sanctions-relief step following the bilateral, would confirm normalisation is real rather than procedural. A one-day attendance with no communique language, no relief and no second invitation means the table was rented for a negotiation, not restored.

brief.h: Beijing's Pacific envoy Qian Bo says "there will always be consequences" after Taiwan's foreign minister attended the Pacific Islands Forum opening in Palau - then adds, "it's not a threat"
brief.t: Qian Bo said "Taiwan is not a dialogue partner with the forum so we have serious concerns" and "we have made our position very clear to the government of Palau and the secretariat," before the line that carries the story: "there will always be consequences - this should not have happened. We think it's very inappropriate." Taiwan's foreign minister Lin Chia-lung attended the opening in Koror with a large business delegation. The detail that matters more than the quote is the seating: the leaders of Fiji, Vanuatu, Samoa, Solomon Islands and Kiribati all sent ministers instead of attending, and New Zealand's foreign minister publicly wondered about "foreign interference" in those absences without naming a country. Palau's president Surangel Whipps Jr answered in kind: "our partners are welcome to sail with us, but they do not choose our destination," and "attention is not the same as respect."
brief.context: Name the mechanism: attendance economics. Beijing does not need Taiwan thrown out of the forum, and trying would fail publicly. It needs enough heads of government to stay home that the forum's communiques stop carrying weight - a body devalued is cheaper to defeat than a body opposed, and it leaves no fingerprints. The rail underneath is two decades of recognition attrition running one way: the Solomon Islands and Kiribati switched in 2019 and Nauru in 2024, leaving Palau, Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands as the last three Pacific states recognising Taipei out of twelve worldwide. Constraint before character applies to Whipps too - his defiance is affordable because Palau's security and budget run through the US Compact of Free Association, and the lever Beijing actually holds over him is Chinese group tourism, which is discretionary, deniable and fast. The deciding desk here is a tour-operator licensing authority, not a foreign ministry.

angles.effect: Gets its demonstration either way. If a measure follows, hosting Taipei is shown to cost; if none does, the ministers who stayed home already delivered the result at no price.
Gain domestic standing and a live argument for larger US compact funding, while carrying whatever the tourism or fisheries consequence turns out to be.
Buys a photograph and business memoranda, not membership. Presence at an opening ceremony is not dialogue-partner status, and the delegation's size is doing the work the diplomatic status cannot.
Pay quietly. A forum whose leaders stop attending loses the collective bargaining power that was the small states' only real leverage against either patron.
Pay in influence they assumed was structural. New Zealand's public suspicion about the absences is an admission that the guest list is no longer theirs to shape.

dec.kill: A named Chinese measure against Palau - a group-tour suspension, an aid pause, a fisheries or customs action within weeks - would convert "consequences" into an instrument and confirm tourism is the operative lever. A forum that issues its communique normally and a Palauan tourist season that opens unchanged means the warning was rhetorical and the absent leaders were the whole play.

brief.h: The Hague tribunal ordered India to keep honouring the Indus Waters Treaty; India replied that the "so-called Court of Arbitration has no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India's sovereign decisions"
brief.t: The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled on Monday that the 1960 treaty "remains fully binding" and that India had no valid grounds to suspend it, and ordered limits on construction at the Ratle hydroelectric project pending a World Bank-appointed neutral expert whose decision is expected by July 2027, with restrictions running 90 days beyond it. India rejected the award outright, calling the court illegally constituted by the World Bank in breach of the treaty's own terms, noting it has never recognised the body in law and has never appeared before it. Pakistan welcomed the interim measures and said it is "carefully considering the details of the decision to determine how it can best assist in finding a pathway back to engagement." The treaty has been in abeyance since April 2025, when India suspended it after the Pahalgam attack killed 26 people.
brief.context: Non-appearance is a strategy, not a snub, and it is the tell. India is not losing this arbitration - it is denying the forum, which is what a state does when it holds the physical asset and expects to keep holding it; the same move Russia made on the Arctic seabed and China made at the South China Sea tribunal, and both awards still stand unenforced. The rail is the treaty's own dispute machinery, the only thing that ever made a water-sharing agreement between two nuclear rivals durable: the Indus system feeds about 80 percent of Pakistan's irrigated farmland, and India sits upstream of all of it. The base rate is the point - the treaty survived the 1965, 1971 and 1999 wars, which is why its suspension, not this ruling, is the actual event. Constraint before character on New Delhi too: India cannot today store or divert the western rivers at scale, so the leverage it has seized is informational rather than volumetric - flood data, reservoir flushing schedules, filling timings - and that is already enough to make a Pakistani planting season a matter of someone else's discretion.

angles.effect: Converts a treaty obligation into a discretionary tap and pays with its own record. A state that has spent two decades arguing for rules-based order has just made non-compliance with a water tribunal look ordinary.
Wins on paper and cannot enforce it. An award against a non-appearing upper riparian is a document, and the cost lands on irrigation planners who must now budget for uncertainty rather than volume.
Loses guarantor credibility on the one treaty where it is named in the text. If its appointed forum can be declared illegally constituted by a party, its other guarantees get read the same way.

Gains the precedent for free - and India is the second-order loser. China sits upstream of the Brahmaputra, and every argument New Delhi makes about sovereign discretion over headwaters is one it will hear repeated back.
Gains construction freedom at Ratle and Kishenganga that the treaty's design constraints denied it for years - the one party with an unambiguous material win.

dec.kill: India starting storage construction or publishing revised designs on the western rivers would convert the leverage from informational to physical and make this a treaty exit. India quietly resuming flood-data sharing, or accepting the neutral expert's process while rejecting only the court, would mean the rejection is jurisdictional lawyering and the treaty is being suspended as pressure rather than abandoned.

lesson: Thomas Schelling's Arms and Influence draws a line that almost every news cycle blurs, and today's board is the cleanest example of it in months. DETERRENCE is telling someone not to start something; it is cheap, because the other side only has to keep doing nothing, and nobody has to be seen backing down. COMPELLENCE is forcing someone to actively stop, undo or hand over something they are already doing — and it is far harder, because it requires a visible climb-down, which is exactly the thing governments cannot afford in front of their own supporters. Schelling's insight was that compellence therefore needs an off-ramp built into the threat: a way for the target to comply that does not look like surrender. Look at what happened here. The Kharg video is a compellent threat — stop mining the strait, reopen it — delivered in a form that gives Tehran no ladder down at all, and the same is true of a weekly sanctions cadence announced in advance, which converts every future pause into a public retreat by the sanctioner. Meanwhile the actual strike was tiny and target-matched, and Iran's reply was fired at forewarned bases and intercepted: both sides operating the deterrence half of the ledger competently while the loud half fails. The falsifiable prediction that follows: over the next three months expect the pattern to hold — small proportionate exchanges that do not escalate, alongside maximal declaratory threats that do not produce Iranian compliance — and if instead Tehran publicly reopens the strait under threat without any face-saving instrument attached, Schelling's rule is failing on this file and we should say so out loud.

lecture.title: The Economic Weapon: Why Sieges Make the Wars They Mean to Prevent

sections.t: Treasury designated roughly sixty Chinese “teapot” refiners — the small plants buying discounted Iranian crude — while touching no Chinese state major and no bank. The same week, central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes of gold in the quarter gold fell over 20%. Two stories, one machine.

sections.h: Follow the money, name the mechanism
sections.t: A reserve manager buying into a 20% drawdown is not trading. He is hedging ACCESS — the risk that an asset held abroad gets switched off by its host government — and gold is the only large reserve asset with no counterparty who can flip that switch. Name the mechanism: the ECONOMIC WEAPON, using the financial plumbing whose hubs one country owns to inflict a siege without laying one. Iran discounts crude to Chinese teapots paying through dollar-touching chains; Treasury designates them; the IRGC's Strait Authority recoups the shortfall in Hormuz tolls. Sanction and gold bar are one transaction seen from two ends.

sections.h: Deep history I — the blockade that became an idea
sections.t: The economic weapon has a birthday and a founding failure. The birthday is November 1806, when Napoleon's Berlin Decrees declared the British Isles blockaded — the Continental System, an attempt to beat a maritime power by closing a continent's markets to it. It succeeded at nothing except generating enforcement. Portugal would not comply, so France invaded in 1807 and got the Peninsular War, the ulcer that bled the Grande Armée for six years. Alexander I quit the system in December 1810 because it was ruining Russian trade, and in 1812 Napoleon marched east to enforce it. The blockade never defeated Britain; it manufactured the two wars that destroyed the blockader. Sanctions require enforcement, and enforcement against a determined leakage path tends toward conquest. The second case mattered because it worked. The Allied blockade of Germany ran from 1914 through the armistice and was lifted only when Germany signed at Versailles in June 1919. German official estimates put civilian deaths from malnutrition near 424,000 — contested, and historians still argue how much was blockade and how much German agricultural mismanagement. But perception makes policy, and a generation concluded hunger had beaten an undefeated army. So they institutionalized it as a PEACE instrument: Article 16 of the League Covenant made sanctions automatic against an aggressor, and Wilson in 1919 put it in words no Treasury official would dare use today — “A nation that is boycotted is a nation that is in sight of surrender. Apply this economic, peaceful, silent, deadly remedy and there will be no need for force.” The weapon was invented to ABOLISH war; the rest of the century refutes that sentence.

sections.h: Deep history II — the failures that define our problem
sections.t: ABYSSINIA, 1935. Italy invaded Ethiopia; the League invoked Article 16 — exempting oil, coal and steel, and never closing the Suez Canal, which Britain controlled and through which Italian troopships sailed. Mussolini won anyway. The sanctions were real enough to enrage and too porous to stop, and the lesson is sharper than “sanctions don't work”: a sanction calibrated to spare the sender teaches the target that the sender is deterred too. Then the second-order effect. Nicholas Mulder's argument in The Economic Weapon is that the interwar regime deterred small states and PROVOKED large ones. Italy, Germany and Japan drew the same conclusion from the 1930s — dependence on seaborne trade was a vulnerability an enemy could switch off at will, and the answer was autarky, self-sufficiency taken by force. Lebensraum and the Co-Prosperity Sphere were ideological projects; they were also sanctions-proofing programs. Japan is the proof case. Washington embargoed scrap iron in 1940, then froze Japanese assets on 26 July 1941; America supplied roughly 80% of Japan's oil, and with Britain and the Dutch East Indies following, Japan lost about 88% of its oil imports. Reserves would last three years at peace, half that at war — Nagano's image was of a patient wasting away, every month of compliance leaving Japan weaker against the enemy it expected to fight. Pearl Harbor came in December. And the detail that turns story into discipline: the freeze was never meant to be total. Roosevelt intended a licensing regime keeping oil flowing so the tap stayed usable as leverage; officials in State and Treasury administered it so strictly that no licences issued and the flow stopped. The sanction that helped produce Pearl Harbor was substantially an organizational outcome, not a presidential decision — Allison's Essence of Decision, live. Before inferring “Iran's strategy” from one action, ask which bureau took it.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: The leakage path is always the whole story — not the designation list, the leak: Portugal and Russia in 1806, Beira and Pretoria in 1966, Chinese teapots now. NOW THE BREAK. Japan in 1941 had a military option that promised to SOLVE its resource problem: seize the Dutch East Indies and own the oil. Iran has none — it fought its war, lost the conventional exchange, and has played its asymmetric card, the Hormuz toll. Nor did 1914 face an alternative supplier: Iran's is the world's second-largest economy, which the sanctioner just spared. Less Pearl Harbor, more Rhodesia.

MULDER says the siege provokes: strangulation drives large states to autarky, then preemption. DREZNER says sanctions are cheap theater — Hufbauer's data give a third success rate at best, near zero against great powers. The 2026 evidence buries neither: it splits by SIDE, and the split is the finding. On the TARGET Mulder scores: gold, stockpiles, payment rails, enrichment acceleration under maximum pressure. On the SENDER Drezner scores harder — the carve-outs. Sixty teapots and not one bank is not escalation; it is the sanctioner taking its own threat hostage, because hitting a Chinese bank endangers the dollar system that makes the hammer heavy.

The 2015 architecture is not coming back (high confidence): the 2022 freeze of Russian reserves turned the settlement network into an instrument; a hedge once bought is not resold. Expect bifurcation, not de-dollarization (moderate-high). EICHENGREEN is right that currencies erode glacially; the WEAPON depreciates faster than the CURRENCY. The bolder call (moderate): the most dangerous decade is the one in which the weapon still works but no longer terrifies. Mulder's mechanism fires in the transition — invested in escaping, not finished, expecting strangulation regardless. For China, the 2030s — so Economic D-Day may SHORTEN the fuse it was meant to lengthen. FALSIFIER: designate a major Chinese state bank; if Beijing cuts Iranian purchases within a quarter, I am wrong. Two centuries say the economic weapon does not replace war — it sorts the world into blocs that survive each other's sieges, then gives the survivors a reason to fight.

Nicholas Mulder, The Economic Weapon (2022) — published weeks before the Russia sanctions matched its template. Farrell & Newman, “Weaponized Interdependence” (2019) — it called the 2022 playbook and the chip controls in advance. Eichengreen, Exorbitant Privilege — the counterweight.
